Neutron stars and black holes are necessary extrapolations of the same principle that makes stars:

  • In a star, gravity forces elements to fuse, which creates radiation pressure that pushes back and prevents complete collapse.

  • In a white dwarf, gravity packs the non-fusing atoms tightly together, with the structure maintained by electrons' repulsion of one another

  • In a neutron star, gravity overcomes the electrons' forces and forces them to fuse with the protons they orbit; after this subatomic fusion, the star's structure is maintained by the incompressability of neutrons

  • In a black hole, gravity overwhelms all repulsive forces that could prevent the structure's collapse, creating a point object and an event horizon that represents the distance from that object that gravity exceeds these limits

If you want to get these "kinks" out of the system, you'd best be prepared to rewrite the book on gravity from the ground up.
